entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10969"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 2</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ezek.2.1-Ezek.2.10">Eze 2:1-10</reference>. Ezekiel's Commission.</title> <div sID="gen19766" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10969"/><hi type="bold">1. Son of man--</hi>often applied to Ezekiel; once only to Daniel (<reference osisRef="Dan.8.17">Da 8:17</reference>), and not to any other prophet. The phrase was no doubt taken from Chaldean usage during the sojourn of Daniel and Ezekiel in Chaldea. But the spirit who sanctioned the words of the prophet implied by it the lowliness and frailty of the prophet as man "lower than the angels," though now admitted to the vision of angels and of God Himself, "lest he should be exalted through the abundance of the revelations" (<reference osisRef="2Cor.12.7">2Co 12:7</reference>). He is appropriately so called as being type of the divine "Son of man" here revealed as "man" (see on <reference osisRef="Ezek.1.26">Eze 1:26</reference>). That title, as applied to Messiah, implies at once His lowliness and His exaltation, in His manifestations as the Representative man, at His first and second comings respectively (<reference osisRef="Ps.8.4-Ps.8.8">Psa 8:4-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.16.13">Mt 16:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.20.18">20:18</reference>; and on the other hand, <reference osisRef="Dan.7.13">Da 7:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Dan.7.14">14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.26.64">Mt 26:64</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.5.27">Joh 5:27</reference>). <div eID="gen19766" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 2 Eze 2:1-10 . Ezekiel's Commission. 1. Son of man-- often applied to Ezekiel; once only to Daniel ( Da 8:17 ), and not to any other prophet. The phrase was no doubt taken from Chaldean usage during the sojourn of Daniel and Ezekiel in Chaldea. But the spirit who sanctioned the words of the prophet implied by it the lowliness and frailty of the prophet as man "lower than the angels," though now admitted to the vision of angels and of God Himself, "lest he should be exalted through the abundance of the revelations" ( 2Co 12:7 ). He is appropriately so called as being type of the divine "Son of man" here revealed as "man" (see on Eze 1:26 ). That title, as applied to Messiah, implies at once His lowliness and His exaltation, in His manifestations as the Representative man, at His first and second comings respectively ( Psa 8:4-8 ; Mt 16:13 ; 20:18 ; and on the other hand, Da 7:13 , 14 ; Mt 26:64 ; Joh 5:27 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10970"/><div sID="gen19767" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10970"/><hi type="bold">2. spirit entered ... when he spake--</hi>The divine word is ever accompanied by the Spirit (<reference osisRef="Gen.1.2">Ge 1:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.3">3</reference>).<div eID="gen19767" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19768" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">set ... upon ... feet--</hi>He had been "upon his face" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.1.28">Eze 1:28</reference>). Humiliation on our part is followed by exaltation on God's part (<reference osisRef="Ezek.3.23">Eze 3:23</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.3.24">24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.22.29">Job 22:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jas.4.6">Jas 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.5.5">1Pe 5:5</reference>). "On the feet" was the fitting attitude when he was called on to walk and work for God (<reference osisRef="Eph.5.8">Ep 5:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.6.15">6:15</reference>).<div eID="gen19768" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19769" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that I heard--</hi>rather, "then I heard." <div eID="gen19769" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 2. spirit entered ... when he spake-- The divine word is ever accompanied by the Spirit ( Ge 1:2 , 3 ). set ... upon ... feet-- He had been "upon his face" ( Eze 1:28 ). Humiliation on our part is followed by exaltation on God's part ( Eze 3:23 , 24 ; Job 22:29 ; Jas 4:6 ; 1Pe 5:5 ). "On the feet" was the fitting attitude when he was called on to walk and work for God ( Ep 5:8 ; 6:15 ). that I heard-- rather, "then I heard."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10976"/><div sID="gen19781" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10976"/><hi type="bold">8. eat--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Jer.15.16">Jr 15:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.10.9">Re 10:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.10.10">10</reference>). The idea is to possess himself fully of the message and digest it in the mind; not literal eating, but such an appropriation of its unsavory contents that they should become, as it were, part of himself, so as to impart them the more vividly to his hearers. <div eID="gen19781" type="x-p"/>
